currentFailure.observed: Current g target reports3passed/1failed. Existing HTTP corrupt-input and original atomic-write/revocation checks reached the final close. Close surfaced Bridge startup task failure reading preferences.json while test immediately wrote invalid JSON after listener on_ready.
currentFailure.classification: Confirmed startup fixture interleaving; prior development passes do not establish deterministic readiness. Preserve g failure and do not weaken close.

causalSource: lib.rs run starts BridgeHost by spawning its task, then invokes listener on_ready without awaiting Bridge initialization.
BridgeHost.run unconditionally begins with bridge_routes::import_existing, which synchronously list_agent_summaries and reads preferences.json, before its recovery awaits.
An immediate post-ready corruption can therefore reach that startup reader; later restoring valid prefs cannot turn its stored task error back into success.
BridgeHost.wait_stopped propagates that task error at original service close; it is not evidence the preference endpoint silently saved damaged input.
existingMarkersRejected: BridgeHost.started means task spawned, not initialization complete.
bridge_routes status bridgeReady=true/bridgeInitializing=false are static values; not a real barrier.
Listener on_ready, health200, a separate agents200, one database read, or a fixed sleep do not prove the Bridge startup task has passed the file read.

recommendedMinimalFixture.where: Only the corrupt-preferences case: seed after bootstrap has created actual storage, before spawning production run. Keep all service components and the actual HTTP listener active. Do not modify frozen g; any implementation is after its complete evidence closure.
steps: Create one uniquely named synthetic connector using put_connector with valid platform, studio, actor label, user_local owner, explicit synthetic owner_sender_id, enabled=true, config_json={}. No platform secret or account.

Using returned generation, claim_inbox with same connector/platform and owner sender, Dm, unique message/conversation id, payload text=/rc, no attachments. Actual store freezes Owner from connector identity; do not forge role fields.
Call claim_command using same generation and rc. Assert claimed true, receipt Started and result None. This records a before-dispatch crash state; do not call any command dispatcher or settle helper.

Before run starts, put_connector with returned expected generation and identical identity but enabled=false. Assert connector disabled and get_command still Started. The generation update only marks status=claimed inbox unknown; this inbox is already status=command, so its Started command receipt stays intact.

Start the unchanged production run and obtain listener address as before. Within a bounded setup wait using an actual condition, poll get_command until status Unknown with exact error: command result unknown after restart; do not execute again. Fail if service task ends, timeout occurs, row is missing or any different terminal state is observed. Do not invoke recover_started_commands from the test.

Only after this observed recovery, write the original damaged preferences variants and retain every original actual HTTP500/unchanged bytes/atomic authorization/temp-file assertion. End via original close and keep outcome/drain assertions unchanged.
recommendedMinimalFixture.whyThisIsReal: Service code has only one call to recover_started_commands, in BridgeHost.run after import_existing and prior recovery steps. Observing a known pre-run Started row transition to Unknown demonstrates the real startup task passed the preference-dependent import; the test does not return a fake ready flag.
recommendedMinimalFixture.whyNoExternalEffect: Connector is disabled before the first host tick; command receipt is only Started, then Unknown, never Confirmed. list_pending_command_replies selects Confirmed only; recovery explicitly refuses re-execution. No Run, session creation, outbox send or SDK worker is needed. claim_inbox allocates a stable session identity string but does not create a sessions record.
additionalGuardFacts: Assert initial Started survives the connector disable before run so recovery cannot be pre-satisfied.
Optionally assert no new run/outbox and disabled connector stays disabled after startup; these verify inert preparation, not new product coverage.
Keep original20s HTTP budget and actual service shutdown assertion; add only bounded condition-based setup wait, not a blind delay.
Retain Bridge host running throughout malformed HTTP checks; no new product/public ready API or host bypass.

alternativeNotChosen: Existing bridge.stop followed by wait_stopped would also await unconditional import on valid prefs, but stops an unrelated component early. Prefer the inert real recovery sentinel to preserve full running-host scope.
